lineItemClassification.instructions: Classify this repair estimate line item given the reported accident (a rear-bumper hit-and-run on a parked car).

criteria.a legitimate repair line item: The item is a fair, market-rate charge for parts or labor needed to repair the damage described in the claim (rear bumper damage from a parking-lot collision).
criteria.an inflated line item: The item is overpriced, padded, or for work far beyond what the described damage requires — e.g. excessive labor hours, OEM pricing for aftermarket parts, or duplicate charges.
criteria.a line item for staged or fabricated dam: The item charges for damage that was deliberately caused or entirely fabricated as part of a staged accident — work with no plausible connection to any real collision.
criteria.a line item for pre-existing damage: The item covers damage that existed before the reported incident — e.g. old scratches on an unrelated panel, wear, or rust repair bundled into the claim.

hasPaintTransfer.instructions: Does the evidence (police report, photos, inspection) show paint transfer or foreign material on the claimant's vehicle indicating another car made contact?

witnessCredibility.instructions: How credible is this witness's account?
criteria: not credible — contradicted by physical evidence or clear motive to lie
weak — vague, uncertain, or with a relationship to the claimant
strong — independent, specific, and consistent with physical evidence

estimateMatchesDamage.instructions: Does every line item in the repair estimate correspond to damage consistent with the reported accident?

priorDamageEvidence.instructions: Is there evidence (pre-incident photos, prior claim records, inspection notes) that any of the claimed damage existed before the incident date?
